data.title: Devín – a Great Moravian palace with a church in 3D
data.excerpt: The masonry building of the 9th century uncovered at Devín is usually reconstructed only as a church with three apses. Its ground plan with several partitions suggests, however, that it may have served two purposes at once, and our 3D reconstruction, made with the archaeologist Július Vavák, shows this palace-and-church arrangement.

mediaTexts.alt: A 3D reconstruction of a Great Moravian palace with a church with a round apse in the evening light

children.text: This time Dwarf digital archeology and Hradiska.sk, in close cooperation with the archaeologist Július Vavák (the Lesser Carpathian Museum in Pezinok, to whom great thanks are hereby due for his valuable expert help throughout the reconstruction), have made an attempt at a 3D reconstruction of the possible appearance of a masonry building from the period of Great Moravia (9th century) which was discovered at the castle of

Some reconstructions are known to the public, but these show the building only as a church with three apses. Its uncovered ground plan, with several partitions, nevertheless suggests that it may in fact have been a building that served two purposes. Part of the building may have served as a church and another part as a palace intended for residential and ceremonial purposes. We have therefore tried to reconstruct the possible appearance of precisely this layout of the building. It may have been here that Prince Rastislav stayed during the siege of Devín by the Frankish army in 864.

blocks.alt: Devín - a Great Moravian palace with a church in 3D

children.text: The website www.apsida.sk gives the following description of the building:

“The rectangular nave, divided by two partitions into two narrow rooms at the sides and one large room in the middle, measures 540 cm x 1,135 cm; adjoining it on the eastern side is a rectangular space terminating in three apses arranged in the shape of a cross, which have a diameter of 330 cm. The width of the foundations is 60–75 cm.

The church was built at some point in the second half of the 9th century, using Roman building material. It is usually dated to the reign of Rastislav, and according to the most recent sources to the period 850–863/870. Given the ground plan formed by four rooms, including the three-apsed eastern end, it is still not entirely clear what kind of building this is. There is no doubt about its sacred purpose, but according to various specialists it may have been a church, or a three-apsed chapel attached to a residential (episcopal) palace; some authors also speak of a so-called triclinium – the audience hall of a church dignitary.

blocks.alt: Devín - a Great Moravian palace with a church in 3D

children.text: The builders of the little church were apparently inspired by the late antique churches of a similar layout in the region of Dalmatia; the Devín church is particularly close to the buildings at Sutivan, Pridraga and Bilice.”
